---
title: "Resources"
order: 100
---

- [45 CFR 164.402 — Definitions (eCFR)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-D/section-164.402) —
  the breach definition, its three exclusions, the presumption-of-breach standard, the
  four-factor risk assessment, and "unsecured protected health information." Start here before
  running the test against any real incident.
- [45 CFR 164.404 — Notification to individuals (eCFR)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-D/section-164.404) —
  the 60-calendar-day clock from discovery and the five required content elements. Use this to
  check a draft notification letter against the actual regulatory checklist.
- [45 CFR 164.406 — Notification to the media (eCFR)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-D/section-164.406) —
  the 500-resident threshold that triggers media notification. Use this to confirm whether a
  given breach's size actually clears the bar before assuming it does.
- [45 CFR 164.408 — Notification to the Secretary (eCFR)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-D/section-164.408) —
  the two HHS notification tracks: contemporaneous for 500+ individuals, annual log for fewer.
  Use this to pick the right track before a filing goes out.
- [Filing a Biological Product Deviation Report](../../fda-and-aabb-in-practice/filing-a-biological-product-deviation-report/index.qmd) —
  this course's internal link back to 606.171's own 45-day BPDR clock and filing mechanics, for
  comparing the two reporting pathways side by side.
- [Federal Register: Modifications to the HIPAA Privacy, Security, Enforcement, and Breach Notification Rules (2013 Omnibus Rule, GovInfo PDF)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2013-01-25/pdf/2013-01073.pdf) —
  the official preamble where HHS explains why it replaced the old "harm" standard with the
  presumption of breach and the four-factor assessment. Read it when you need the regulator's own
  reasoning for how to weigh a factor. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- [Cornell LII: 45 CFR 164.414 — Administrative requirements and burden of proof](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.414) —
  a second, plain-text view of the burden-of-proof provision the lesson leans on, handy for pasting
  an exact citation into a risk-assessment record. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- [HHS OCR Breach Portal ("Wall of Shame")](https://ocrportal.hhs.gov/ocr/breach/breach_report.jsf) —
  OCR's own public list of reported breaches affecting 500 or more individuals; it is also where
  breach reports are filed. Browse it to see what the 164.408(b) track looks like in practice.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- [NIST SP 800-111: Guide to Storage Encryption Technologies for End User Devices](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/111/final) —
  the federal reference on full-disk encryption for laptops. Read it for what "confirmed
  encryption" means technically, the premise factor 3 turned on. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- [FDA: Biological Product Deviations](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/report-problem-center-biologics-evaluation-research/biological-product-deviations) —
  FDA/CBER's own page on BPDR reporting, the other side of this lesson's dual-reporting
  comparison. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- [HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (for managers)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JwIIP4uBiyA)
  (JurisIQ Learning Center, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson: an
  attorney-led training presentation on the Breach Notification Rule. Legal-training content, not
  HHS/OCR (no OCR video on breach notification itself was found), not blood-specific, and silent on
  FDA reporting. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

hhs.gov's own breach-notification pages returned HTTP 403 to automated checks, so they are not
linked here; reach them from OCR's site in a browser.
